name: Robot fleet supervisor
oneLiner: Every robot that arrives creates people who watch, fix and redirect it. The fleet-scale version of that shift has no title yet.
why: Employers expect robots to displace more work than they create — and deployed fleets need supervision, maintenance and exception handling
The nearest existing job, industrial machinery mechanic, already carries a strong official projection
threats: Robots that maintain robots would hollow the role from underneath
The work may stay distributed across existing technician jobs rather than becoming a title

claims.text: McKinsey estimates robots reach about 13% of US work hours today, against 44% for software agents — the physical fleet is early, and supervised by people where it exists.

In the WEF employer survey, robotics engineers are among the fastest-growing roles, while robots and autonomous systems are the one technology driver expected to displace more jobs than they create by 2030 — a net −5 million.
